mainTopic: מעשר שני as מצה: רב אסי's ownership rule, ריש לקיש's question about חלה of מעשר שני, and the start of the תודה and נזיר loaves
overview: The amud continues רב אסי's statement. רבי מאיר holds that מעשר שני belongs to Heaven, while חכמים hold that it belongs to the person. רב אסי applies this disagreement to מצה on פסח and to an אתרוג on סוכות. רב פפא objects: the Torah says 'yours' for dough and for אתרוג, but never 'your מצה.' רבא answers with a גזירה שוה on the word 'לחם,' which links מצה to חלה, so מצה must also be yours. A ברייתא about dough of מעשר שני is offered as possible support, and the גמרא explains why it is only a 'maybe.' Next, ריש לקיש asks whether חלה taken from מעשר שני dough can be used as מצה. The question is narrowed step by step and turns on the 'הואיל' argument, and רבא resolves it by ruling that all מעשר is one category. The amud ends as the גמרא begins to find the source for why חלות תודה and רקיקי נזיר do not work as מצה, and the verse comes on the next amud.

steps.title: מצה made from מעשר שני produce
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי continues his statement and rules on מצה baked from מעשר שני flour. According to רבי מאיר, a person does not fulfill the מצוה of eating מצה with it. According to חכמים, he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: מצות made from מעשר שני: according to רבי מאיר, a person does not fulfill his obligation with it on פסח. According to חכמים, he does fulfill his obligation with it on פסח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי takes the dispute about whether a person owns מעשר שני and applies it to eating מצה on the night of פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds that מעשר שני is ממון גבוה, so it is not really yours, and he assumes the מצה must be yours. חכמים hold it is ממון הדיוט, so the person owns it and the מצה is fine. Keep in mind that the ruling here depends on ownership. רב פפא will question exactly that link.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, produce that must be eaten in ירושלים in purity
Fulfills his obligation
A תנא who holds מעשר שני is ממון גבוה (belongs to Heaven)
The majority of Sages, who hold מעשר שני is ממון הדיוט (belongs to the person)

steps.confusionAlert: Nobody is saying the מצה is not real מצה. The only question is whether something that is not fully 'yours' can be used for the מצוה.

phrases.english: Matzot made of second-tithe produce,
according to the words of Rabbi Meir —
phrases.notes: He views מעשר שני as belonging to Heaven

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהּ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח,
phrases.english: a person does not fulfill his obligation with it on Pesach;
according to the words of the Rabbis —
he fulfills his obligation with it on Pesach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב אסי's statement from the previous amud, which applied the same dispute to dough and חלה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצה of מעשר שני: רבי מאיר says it is invalid for the מצוה; חכמים say it is valid.

steps.title: אתרוג from מעשר שני produce
steps.stepSummary: The same dispute is applied to an אתרוג of מעשר שני on the first day of סוכות. רבי מאיר says it is invalid and חכמים say it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: An אתרוג of מעשר שני: according to רבי מאיר, one does not fulfill his obligation with it on יום טוב. According to חכמים, a person does fulfill his obligation with it on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי continues and applies the same ownership dispute to the אתרוג used for ארבעה מינים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first day of סוכות the ארבעה מינים must belong to you. Whether an אתרוג of מעשר שני works therefore depends on whether you own it. This is the same split as in the מצה case.

keyTerms.meaning: Citron, one of the ארבעה מינים
The festival; here, the first day of סוכות

phrases.english: A citron of second-tithe produce,
according to the words of Rabbi Meir —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין יוֹצֵא בּוֹ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: one does not fulfill his obligation with it on the festival;
according to the words of the Rabbis —

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם יוֹצֵא בּוֹ יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בְּיוֹם טוֹב.
phrases.english: a person fulfills his obligation with it on the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel case in the same statement of רב אסי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אתרוג of מעשר שני: רבי מאיר says it is invalid on the first day of יום טוב; חכמים say it is valid.
steps.whyThisMatters: רב אסי treats מצה and אתרוג as the same kind of case. רב פפא is about to argue that they are not.

steps.title: רב פפא grants the dough and אתרוג cases
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא opens his objection by accepting two of the cases. For dough, the פסוק says 'your dough.' For אתרוג, it says 'for yourselves.' In both, the Torah clearly requires ownership.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא objected: It makes sense for dough, since it is written 'your dough,' meaning from what is yours. The אתרוג too, since it is written 'And you shall take for yourselves,' and 'for yourselves' means it must be from what is yours.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא begins a challenge. This step only sets it up: he first lists the cases that make sense, so he can then point to the one that does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בִּשְׁלָמָא means 'granted.' It signals that he accepts these cases before attacking another one. For חלה and for אתרוג, the Torah's wording ('your,' 'for yourselves') gives a clear reason why ownership matters.

keyTerms.meaning: Strongly objects to it
Granted / it is understandable that
'Your dough' (במדבר ט״ו), the source for חלה
'And you shall take for yourselves' (ויקרא כ״ג), the source for ארבעה מינים
From what belongs to you

phrases.english: Rav Pappa strongly objected to this:
Granted, with regard to dough,
since it is written 'your dough' — from what is yours.
The etrog too,
since it is written 'And you shall take for yourselves,'
'for yourselves' — it must be from what is yours.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא: בִּשְׁלָמָא עִיסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an attack on רב אסי's statement by accepting its other cases.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's ruling on מצה of מעשר שני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the cases with explicit 'your' wording are accepted, so that the contrast with מצה becomes clear.

steps.title: But the Torah never says 'your מצה'
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא makes his challenge. No פסוק says 'your מצה.' Why, then, should ownership matter for the מצה case according to רבי מאיר?
steps.simpleTranslation: But מצה — is it written 'your מצה'?
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual challenge. The ownership rule has a source for dough and for אתרוג, but there is no such source for מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Torah does not require that the מצה be yours, then whether מעשר שני is ממון גבוה should make no difference. Even רבי מאיר should allow the מצה. רב אסי's ruling on מצה now seems to have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: But (introduces the contrasting problem case)
Is it written? (a rhetorical challenge)
'Your מצה' (a phrase that does not appear in the Torah)

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא argues that the ownership requirement must come from a פסוק. Dough has one ('עריסותיכם') and אתרוג has one ('לכם'), but מצה has none. So the dispute about owning מעשר שני should not affect מצה.
steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about whether the מצה is kosher. It asks only why רבי מאיר should disqualify it, since the Torah never says the מצה must be 'yours.'

phrases.english: But matzah,
is it written 'your matzah'?
phrases.notes: He's asking it to make a point: the פסוק doesn't actually say that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge that step 3 set up.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's claim that, according to רבי מאיר, one does not fulfill the obligation with מצה of מעשר שני
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Ownership is required only where the Torah says 'yours.' The Torah has no 'your מצה,' so ownership should be irrelevant to מצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next part of the sugya. The גמרא will now need to find a different source that disqualifies מצה of מעשר שני.

steps.title: Learning ownership for מצה from the word 'bread'
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רב יימר בר שלמיא) answers רב פפא with a גזירה שוה. The word 'לחם' appears both by מצה and by חלה. Just as חלה applies only to what is yours, מצה must also be yours.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say רב יימר בר שלמיא said: We learn it from 'bread' and 'bread.' Here, by מצה, it says 'poor man's bread.' There, by חלה, it says 'when you eat of the bread of the land.' Just as there it must be from what is yours, so too here it must be from what is yours.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב פפא's question from Step 4. There is no פסוק saying 'your מצה,' but a matching word teaches the same rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא was right that no פסוק says 'your מצה.' רבא links the word 'לחם' in the מצה פסוק to the same word in the חלה פסוק. Since חלה requires ownership ('your dough'), מצה gets the same requirement. So according to רבי מאיר, מעשר שני flour does not work, because he holds מעשר שני is not fully yours.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It comes' — we learn it through a word comparison
'Poor man's bread' — the Torah's name for מצה
'Bread of the land' — from the פסוק about חלה
'Just as there, so too here' — the formula that transfers a rule
'From what is yours' — owned by you

steps.whyThisMatters: This גזירה שוה is the source that makes ownership a real requirement for מצה according to רבי מאיר.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב יֵימַר בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא:
phrases.english: Rava said, and some say Rav Yeimar bar Shelamya said:
It is learned from 'bread' and 'bread.'
phrases.notes: This is a גזירה שוה: the same word shows up in two places, so we learn one from the other.

phrases.english: It is written here: 'poor man's bread,'
phrases.notes: This פסוק is about מצה (דברים טז:ג).

phrases.english: and it is written there: 'And when you eat of the bread of the land.'
phrases.notes: This פסוק is about חלה (במדבר טו:יט).

phrases.english: Just as there, it must be from what is yours,
so too here, it must be from what is yours.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's objection by supplying a source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With no 'your מצה' in the פסוק, ownership should not matter
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לחם' links מצה to חלה, so מצה must be yours

steps.title: A ברייתא about חלה from מעשר שני dough offered as support
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a ברייתא supports the view that, according to רבי מאיר, מעשר שני is not 'yours.' רבי מאיר says מעשר שני dough is exempt from חלה. חכמים say it is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports him: Dough of מעשר שני is exempt from חלה. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say it is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to back up the earlier ruling (רב אסי's) on מצה of מעשר שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי מאיר exempts מעשר שני dough from חלה, it is because he holds the dough is not 'yours.' That fits the ruling that, for רבי מאיר, מעשר שני מצה does not work. חכמים, who say it is yours, obligate it in חלה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let us say it supports him' — a suggested proof
Dough
Exempt from separating חלה
Obligated

phrases.english: Let us say this supports him:

phrases.aramaic: עִיסָּה שֶׁל מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי פְּטוּרָה מִן הַחַלָּה,
phrases.english: Dough of second tithe is exempt from challah,
the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say: It is obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks for a ברייתא that supports the dispute about מצה of מעשר שני
steps.raayaObject: רב אסי's statement that רבי מאיר and חכמים disagree about dough, מצה and אתרוג of מעשר שני
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: מעשר שני dough is exempt from חלה per רבי מאיר

steps.title: Why only 'let us say'? It is the same thing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised that the ברייתא is presented as only a possible support. It seems to say exactly the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Let us say it supports'?! This is the very same thing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the wording of Step 6. Why call it a 'maybe' when the ברייתא seems identical?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא about dough says word for word what רב אסי himself said about dough. So it is not just a possible support; it is the very same statement. The גמרא asks why it used the hesitant word 'לימא.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is that very thing' — the two are identical

phrases.english: 'Let us say it supports'?!
It is the very same thing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the tentative wording of the proof
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא is identical to the claim, it is a clear proof, not a 'maybe'

steps.title: The real question: does the dough dispute extend to the other cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what 'לימא' meant. Since רבי מאיר and חכמים argue about dough, perhaps they also argue the same way about מצה and אתרוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: Let us say that since they argue about dough, they also argue about these other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains Step 6. The proof is tentative because it is about dough, while the question is about מצה and אתרוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only shows a dispute about חלה. The suggestion is that the same dispute carries over to מצה and אתרוג. That carry-over is not certain, so the proof is only a 'maybe.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means' — explaining an earlier statement
'Since they argue'
'In these too' — the other cases

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
Let us say that since they argue about dough,
they also argue about these other cases.
phrases.notes: These other cases are the מצה and אתרוג of מעשר שני.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the word 'לימא'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the scope of the proposed proof
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is identical to the claim
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about dough. The question is whether the dispute extends to מצה and אתרוג

steps.title: Maybe dough is different: 'your dough' is written twice
steps.stepSummary: Or perhaps dough is a special case. The Torah writes 'עריסותיכם' twice, so ownership there may be stricter. Then the dispute would not carry over to מצה and אתרוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is different there, because 'your dough, your dough' is written twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the doubt. This is why the ברייתא is only a possible support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double 'your dough' may make ownership especially required for חלה. So רבי מאיר could exempt מעשר שני dough from חלה and still allow מעשר שני מצה and אתרוג. The ברייתא therefore does not prove the rule for מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Or perhaps' — raising the other possibility
'It is different there'
'Your dough' — the word in the חלה פסוקים
Twice

steps.confusionAlert: This does not take back רבא's גזירה שוה. It only says the dough ברייתא, by itself, cannot prove the מצה case.
steps.whatToRemember: The dough ברייתא is only a 'maybe' support. חלה may be uniquely strict about ownership, because 'עריסותיכם' appears twice.

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is different there,
since it is written 'your dough,' 'your dough,' two times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the explanation by giving the reason the carry-over may fail
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects treating the dough ברייתא as a definite proof for מצה and אתרוג
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חלה has a doubled ownership word, so its rule may be unique

steps.title: ריש לקיש asks about חלה of מעשר שני as מצה
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן לקיש asks a question. Can a person fulfill the מצוה of eating מצה with חלה separated from מעשר שני dough in ירושלים?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש asked: May a person fulfill his obligation with חלה of מעשר שני in ירושלים?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. It is about the piece of חלה taken from מעשר שני dough, eaten as מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This חלה carries two kinds of holiness at once: מעשר שני and חלה, which is like תרומה. ריש לקיש asks whether this double holiness stops it from counting as מצה. 'In ירושלים' is mentioned because that is where מעשר שני may be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He asked' — raised a question (בעיא)
His obligation (here, eating מצה)
חלה separated from מעשר שני dough

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish asked:
What is the law: may a person fulfill his obligation
with challah of second tithe in Jerusalem?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question about מצה and sanctified produce
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether חלה from מעשר שני dough is valid for the מצוה of מצה

steps.title: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי there is no question
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי the answer is obvious. He holds that even the ordinary, non-חלה part of מעשר שני cannot be used for מצה. Surely its חלה cannot be used either.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, do not ask. Now, if one cannot fulfill with the regular part, must we even ask about its חלה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows ריש לקיש's question. It shows the question cannot be asked according to רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי requires מצה to be food that may be eaten by an אונן (a mourner before burial), and מעשר שני is forbidden to an אונן. So even the regular part of מעשר שני dough is invalid. The חלה, which has even more holiness, is certainly invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: 'According to' the view of
'Do not ask' — the question does not arise
Regular portion (here, the non-חלה part of the מעשר שני dough)
'Is it even a question?' — an obvious קל וחומר

phrases.aramaic: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי — לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ,
phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, do not ask,
for now, if with the regular portion one does not fulfill,
phrases.notes: The regular portion is the part of the מעשר שני dough that isn't חלה.

phrases.english: is it even a question with its challah?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי — לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of ריש לקיש's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: According to רבי יוסי הגלילי, it is clearly invalid, by a קל וחומר from the regular part of the dough

steps.title: The question applies according to רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that ריש לקיש's question is asked according to רבי עקיבא. רבי עקיבא allows מצה from מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: When you ask, ask according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. It tells us which opinion ריש לקיש's question follows, and prepares the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא allows מעשר שני מצה, so the regular part of the dough is fine. The open question is whether the added חלה holiness, on top of מעשר שני, makes it invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When you ask' — this is where the question applies

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא.
phrases.english: When you ask, it is according to Rabbi Akiva.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the narrowing by naming the opinion where the question applies
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ריש לקיש's question is asked according to רבי עקיבא, who allows מעשר שני מצה

steps.title: First side: maybe only the ordinary part of מעשר שני works
steps.stepSummary: The ordinary part of מעשר שני can be redeemed and eaten anywhere if it becomes impure, so it works for מצה. חלה that becomes impure must be burned, so maybe it does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: Maybe it is only with the ordinary part that a person fulfills the מצוה. That is because if it becomes impure, it can be permitted to be eaten anywhere. But חלה, if it becomes impure, cannot be permitted anywhere and goes to be burned. So with it, a person does not fulfill the מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to spell out ריש לקיש's question. This is the first side of the question: maybe חלה from מעשר שני dough does NOT work for מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא allows מעשר שני for מצה because it is not stuck forever with its restrictions. If it becomes impure, it can be redeemed and then eaten in any town (בכל מושבות). חלה has no such escape route, since impure חלה is simply burned. So maybe it fails רבי עקיבא's requirement that the מצה be food that can be permitted in all dwelling places.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, non-holy food. Here it means the regular part of the dough, not the חלה portion.
They became ritually impure.
Permission to be eaten in any dwelling place, not only in ירושלים.
Burning. Impure חלה must be burned.
He fulfills his obligation.

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'חולין' does not mean food that was never holy. It means the regular, non-חלה part of the מעשר שני dough, as opposed to the חלה portion.

phrases.english: It is with the ordinary part that one fulfills the obligation
for if they become impure
they can be permitted in all dwelling places
phrases.notes: Impure מעשר שני may be redeemed, and then the money is used in ירושלים while the food is eaten anywhere.

phrases.english: But חלה, which if it becomes impure
cannot be permitted in any dwelling place
and goes to burning — one does not fulfill the obligation with it

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the first side of ריש לקיש's question, which step 12 placed according to רבי עקיבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the fact that impure חלה cannot be redeemed (only burned) disqualify it for מצה, even though plain מעשר שני is allowed?

steps.title: Second side: the 'הואיל' argument
steps.stepSummary: Maybe we say: had this dough not been named חלה, it could have been redeemed if it became impure. So it still works for מצה now.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps we say: since, if he had not called it by the name חלה and it had become impure, it would have permission to be eaten anywhere, and he could fulfill the מצוה with it, then now too he fulfills the מצוה with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the question. Maybe חלה from מעשר שני dough DOES work for מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is 'הואיל', meaning 'since it could have been'. The dough was able to be redeemed until the person chose to name it חלה. That earlier potential is enough to keep it valid for מצה. Naming it חלה does not erase what the dough itself basically is.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps. This introduces the other side of a question.
Since. A logic of 'since it could have been permitted, it counts as permitted'.
Called a name on it. Here it means designating the dough as חלה.
Now too.

steps.whyThisMatters: The 'הואיל' argument is a well-known pattern across ש״ס. A status that could easily have been in place is treated as if it is in place.

phrases.english: Or perhaps we say:

phrases.aramaic: הוֹאִיל וְאִילּוּ לֹא קָרָא עָלֶיהָ שֵׁם
phrases.english: since, if he had not designated it by name (as חלה)
and it had become impure, it would be permitted in all dwelling places
and one would fulfill the obligation with it
now too one fulfills the obligation

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposite side of the question begun in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do we apply 'הואיל' to treat the חלה as redeemable, based on what the dough could have been before it was designated?

steps.title: Second version: the question is really about dough bought with מעשר שני money
steps.stepSummary: A different version says 'הואיל' surely applies to plain מעשר שני dough. The real question is about חלה from dough that was bought with מעשר שני money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: about this case, you certainly should not ask, because we certainly say 'הואיל'. When you should ask is about חלה of dough bought with מעשר שני money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of ריש לקיש's question. That version moves the question to a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the 'הואיל' logic from step 14 is obvious for plain מעשר שני dough, so there is nothing to ask. The doubt moves to dough that was bought with מעשר שני money, which has a weaker connection to the original מעשר. Whether such food could be redeemed if impure is itself debated, as the next step shows.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say. This introduces a second version of the discussion.
Do not ask it. It is not a question.
Bought with מעשר שני money, after the produce was redeemed for coins.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question that comes after the first one. It is a different version of the same question. In this version, the first case is too easy to ask about.

phrases.english: Some say:
this case you certainly should not ask about
because we certainly say 'since'
When you should ask
is about חלה of dough bought with מעשר שני money

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: הָא וַדַּאי לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second version that treats step 14's 'הואיל' as obvious and moves the question to a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can חלה from dough bought with מעשר שני money be used for מצה?

steps.title: The question only works according to רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: According to the רבנן, food bought with מעשר שני money can be redeemed if it becomes impure, so it is just like מעשר שני and there is no question. The question exists only according to רבי יהודה, who says such food must be buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the רבנן, you should not ask. Since they say it is redeemed, it is just like מעשר. When you should ask is according to רבי יהודה, who says it must be buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows the question even further. It shows which opinion makes the question a real one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known argument about food bought with מעשר שני money that became impure. The רבנן say it is redeemed, so it behaves exactly like מעשר שני, and the 'הואיל' answer works. רבי יהודה says it must be buried, so even before it was named חלה it could never have been redeemed. That makes it unclear whether it still works for מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the opinion of the חכמים (the רבנן).
It is redeemed.
That is the same as מעשר itself.
It must be buried. It cannot be redeemed or eaten.

steps.whatToRemember: Final version of the question: חלה from dough bought with מעשר שני money, according to רבי עקיבא, together with רבי יהודה. According to רבי יהודה, such food that becomes impure is buried, not redeemed.

phrases.english: And according to the רבנן, you should not ask
since they say it is redeemed
it is the same as מעשר itself

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ, אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: When you should ask is according to רבי יהודה
who says it must be buried
phrases.notes: This refers to food bought with מעשר שני money that became impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows step 15's question to the opinion of רבי יהודה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: According to רבי יהודה, where bought food that becomes impure cannot be redeemed, does חלה from such dough still work for מצה?

steps.title: The source for the disagreement about food bought with מעשר שני money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. If food bought with מעשר שני money becomes impure, the רבנן say it is redeemed. רבי יהודה says it must be buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: Food that was bought with מעשר שני money and then became impure should be redeemed. רבי יהודה says: It should be buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for what it just said in Step 16. That step claimed that the רבנן and רבי יהודה argue about impure food bought with מעשר שני money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, bought food acts just like real מעשר שני. It can be redeemed when impure, so there is no question about using it for מצה. רבי יהודה says bought food is weaker and must be buried, so for him the question of ריש לקיש is real.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned (in a משנה)
Food bought with מעשר שני money
It should be redeemed for money
It should be buried

phrases.english: As we learned: that which was bought with second-tithe money
that became impure should be redeemed.
phrases.notes: The redemption money is then used to buy other food to eat in ירושלים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: It should be buried.
phrases.notes: Bought food is a step removed from real מעשר, so its holiness cannot pass on to something else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the משנה source for the claim in Step 16 that the question applies only according to רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן and רבי יהודה disagree about whether impure food bought with מעשר שני money can be redeemed
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה about הלקוח בכסף מעשר שני

steps.title: First side: two 'since' arguments allow it
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps we say two הואיל arguments together. If the dough had not been bought with מעשר money, and had not been named חלה, it could be redeemed when impure. So it works for מצה now too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we say this? Since it would be different if it were not bought with מעשר money, and since it would be different if he had not named it חלה, if it then became impure it could be redeemed and eaten anywhere. That is why one fulfills the מצוה with it in that case, so now too he fulfills the מצוה with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the first side of the question. Maybe we may stack two 'הואיל' arguments, so this חלה works for מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two things stop this dough from being redeemable: it was bought with מעשר money, which matters for רבי יהודה, and it was named חלה. Each problem needs its own 'הואיל' to remove it. If both are removed in our minds, the dough is plain redeemable מעשר שני, which works for מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since': reasoning that judges something by the status it could have had
Bought (with מעשר money)
He gave it a name, meaning he set it aside as חלה
Permitted to be eaten anywhere (after redemption)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two separate 'הואיל' arguments here. One removes the 'bought' problem and one removes the 'חלה' problem. Keep them apart, because the next step asks whether two may be combined.

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן: הוֹאִיל וְאִי לָא לָקוּחַ הָוֵי,
phrases.english: Do we say: since, if it were not bought,

phrases.aramaic: וְהוֹאִיל וְלֹא קָרָא עָלֶיהָ שֵׁם וְאִיטַּמַּי —
phrases.english: and since, if he had not named it (as חלה) and it became impure,
it would be permitted in all places of habitation,

phrases.aramaic: וְנָפֵיק בֵּיהּ, הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי נָפֵיק בֵּיהּ.
phrases.english: and one fulfills the obligation with it, so now too one fulfills the obligation with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the question of ריש לקיש according to רבי יהודה, now with two 'הואיל' arguments needed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Can two 'הואיל' arguments be combined so the חלה works for מצה?

steps.title: Second side: maybe only one 'since' is allowed
steps.stepSummary: Or perhaps we use one הואיל but not two. Then this חלה would not work for מצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps we say one 'since', but we do not say two 'since' arguments?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of the question. Maybe stacking two 'what if' arguments goes too far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One 'הואיל' changes a single fact in our minds. Changing two facts moves us too far from the real case. If only one is allowed, this חלה from bought מעשר food would fail as מצה according to רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps
One 'since' argument
Two 'since' arguments

phrases.english: Or perhaps we say one 'since',
but two 'since' arguments we do not say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided question begun in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether there is a limit of one 'הואיל' per case

steps.title: רבא: all מעשר is one category
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the name מעשר is a single category. Bought food and real מעשר are the same, so only one 'הואיל' is needed and the מצה works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It makes sense that the name 'מעשר' is one thing.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves the question of ריש לקיש. He rules that one fulfills the מצוה with this חלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not need to decide whether two 'הואיל' arguments may be combined. He says food bought with מעשר money is not a separate category from real מעשר, so the 'bought' issue needs no 'הואיל'. Only the חלה issue is left, and one 'הואיל' covers it.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, it is logical
The status or name of מעשר
It is one (single category)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, real מעשר שני and food bought with its money are one category of מעשר. So חלה taken from either kind of dough works as מצה, and only one 'הואיל' is needed.

phrases.english: Rava said: It stands to reason
that the name of מעשר is one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided question of Steps 18-19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: All מעשר, bought or real, is one category, so one 'הואיל' is enough and one fulfills the מצוה.

steps.title: Source for excluding חלות תודה and רקיקי נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה: חלות תודה and רקיקי נזיר made for oneself do not work for מצה. It asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The loaves of a thanksgiving offering and the wafers of a נזיר', and so on. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic. It quotes a new line of the משנה and asks for its source, which sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaves of a תודה and the wafers of a נזיר are made of מצה. Even so, the משנה says that if a person made them for his own offering, he cannot use them for his מצה on פסח. The גמרא wants to know which verse teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: Loaves brought with a thanksgiving offering
Thin wafers brought by a נזיר
From where are these things known?

phrases.english: The loaves of a thanks-offering and wafers of a nazirite, etc.
phrases.notes: A quote of the משנה, opening a new section.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חלה and מעשר שני discussion and moves to the next ruling in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The verse that excludes חלות תודה and רקיקי נזיר from the מצוה of מצה

steps.title: רבה begins his answer with a verse
steps.stepSummary: רבה starts to answer: 'Because the verse says...' The verse itself comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Because the verse says...
steps.whatsHappening: רבה begins to give the source. The actual verse is quoted on the next amud, so this line sets up that answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer will be a פסוק, not a logical argument. It will show that מצה for פסח must be made for the purpose of the מצוה of מצה, not for a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Because the verse says

phrases.english: Rabba said: As the verse states:
phrases.notes: The verse continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to answer the source question of Step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is a verse, which is quoted on the next amud.
